title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, pass on what people said, react like a Sindhi and keep a chat going.
intro:
Half of real conversation is telling each other what happened — and reacting to it. In this unit you learn to tell a friend a story from your own day with the right linking words (**پهريان** 'first', **پوءِ** 'then', **اوچتو** 'suddenly', **آخرڪار** 'in the end'), to say what people said with **ته** (**چيائين ته رستي ۾ آهيان** 'he said he's on his way'), and to describe people and places with Sindhi's paired **relative clauses** (**جيڪو … سو** 'the one who … he').

You'll also pick up the small words that keep a chat alive: **سچي؟** 'really?', **ويچارو!** 'poor guy!', **ڀلا** 'so…', **يعني** 'you mean…', **چرچو ٿو ڪرين؟** 'are you kidding?' — and the great Sindhi pastime, the **ڪچهري**: sitting together for hours just talking.

vocab.note: f · pl ڳالهيون ɠālhyūṃ. ڇا ڳالهه آهي؟ = what's up? / what's the matter?; ڳالهه ڪرڻ = to talk.

vocab.en: story; the whole business, what happened
vocab.note: m. ڇا قصو آهي؟ = what's going on?; وڏو قصو آهي = it's a long story.
Also said انڪري inkare. Comes at the start of the result: بس نه آئي، انهيءَ ڪري دير ٿي.
کل khila (f) = a laugh: مون کي کل اچي وئي = I burst out laughing.
روئڻ لڳي = she started crying.
The everyday Sindhi 'really?' among friends: سچي؟ Also as an oath: سچي ٿو چوان = I'm telling the truth.
A little more neutral than سچي؛ fine with anyone: واقعي؟
Praise and delight: واهه! ڇا ڳالهه آهي! Also sarcastic: واهه، ڏاڍو سٺو! = oh great.
m. ڪمال آهي! = amazing!; ڪمال جو ماڻهو = an amazing person.
Does not change for gender: عجيب ماڻهو، عجيب ڳالهه.
f ويچاري vichārī, pl ويچارا vichārā. Said alone as a reaction: ويچارو! = poor guy!
m. ڏاڍو افسوس ٿيو = I'm so sorry to hear that.
f جيڪا jekā, pl جيڪي jeke; oblique جنهن janhin (pl جن jin). Paired with سو / اهو in the next clause.
f سا sā, pl سي se. At the start of a sentence it also means 'so': سو، مان هليو ويس.
Paired with تڏهن or ته: جڏهن … تڏهن … The question 'when?' is ڪڏهن.
تڏهن ته! = that explains it! / no wonder!
جيئن تون چوين = whatever you say (informal).
Past سڃاتو sañāto: مون کيس ڪونه سڃاتو = I didn't recognise him.

vocab.en: to find out, come to know
vocab.note: Dative + خبر پئي (خبر is f): مون کي خبر پئي = I found out. توکي ڪيئن خبر پئي؟ = how did you find out?
Very Sindhi. هرو ڀرو پريشان نه ٿيو = don't worry for nothing.
m. قسم سان! = I swear! Also خدا جو قسم.
m. منهنجو مطلب آهي ته … = what I mean is …; alone at the start: مطلب، … = I mean, …
Opens a question softly: ڀلا، ڇا ٿيو؟ = so, what happened?
m. Between friends of either sex: ڇڏ يار! Not to elders or strangers — use ادا / ادي / سائين.

vocab.en: a long, relaxed chat; get-together for talking
vocab.note: f. ڪچهري ڪرڻ = to sit and chat. A Sindhi institution: friends, tea and talk late into the night.
m · pl چرچا charchā. چرچو ڪرڻ = to joke, kid. Also مذاق mazāq.

phrases.roman: jeko māṇhū kālha āyo ho, so munhinjo chācho āhe.

He said he's on his way.

phrases.roman: asula meṃ ɠālhi hīa āhe ta…

phrases.roman: ɓudhu na, hika mazedāra ɠālhi ɓudhāyāṃ.
phrases.en: Listen, let me tell you something funny. (informal)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: جيڪو … سو, جتي … اتي, جڏهن … تڏهن
grammar.body:
English puts 'who / where / when' inside the sentence: 'the man **who came yesterday** is my uncle'. Sindhi instead says it in **two halves**: first a clause with a **j-word**, then a clause that starts with a matching word pointing back to it:

**جيڪو … سو** — (the one) who … he: **جيڪو** ماڻهو ڪالهه آيو هو، **سو** منهنجو چاچو آهي.
**جيڪا … سا** (f) · **جيڪي … سي** (pl). In speech the second word is often **اهو / اها / اهي** instead of سو / سا / سي.
**جتي … اتي** — where … there
**جڏهن … تڏهن** (or **ته**) — when … then
**جيئن … تيئن** — as … so

**Agreement:** the j-word agrees with the noun it describes: **جيڪا** ڇوڪري (f), **جيڪي** ماڻهو (pl).

**Before a postposition** the j-word takes its oblique form, **جنهن** (pl **جن**): **جنهن** فلم جي مون ڳالهه ڪئي هئي 'the film (that) I talked about'; **جنهن** سان تون ڳالهائي رهيو هئين 'the one you were talking to'.

**Whatever / whoever:** جيڪو ٿيو، سو ٿيو 'what's done is done'; جيڪو وڻي، سو وٺو 'take whatever you like'.

**Trap:** don't use the question words ڪير / ڪٿي / ڪڏهن here — 'when I was little' is **جڏهن** مان ننڍو هوس, never ڪڏهن.

examples.native: جيڪو ماڻهو دروازي تي آهي، سو ڪير آهي؟
examples.roman: jeko māṇhū darvāze te āhe, so ker āhe?
examples.en: Who's the man at the door? (lit. the man who is at the door, who is he?)

examples.native: جيڪا ڇوڪري ڳائي پئي، سا منهنجي ڀيڻ آهي.
examples.roman: jekā chhokirī ɠāe paī, sā munhinjī bheṇa āhe.
examples.en: The girl who's singing is my sister.

examples.native: جتي ڪالهه ماني کاڌي هئي، اتي ئي هلون؟
examples.roman: jite kālha mānī khādhī huī, ute ī halūṃ?
examples.en: Shall we go to the same place we ate yesterday?

examples.native: جڏهن مان ننڍو هوس، تڏهن ڳوٺ ۾ رهندو هوس.
examples.roman: jaɗahiṃ māṃ nanḍho hos, taɗahiṃ ɠoṭha meṃ rahando hos.
examples.en: When I was little, I used to live in the village. (man)

examples.native: جنهن فلم جي مون ڳالهه ڪئي هئي، اها هيءَ آهي.
examples.roman: janhin filma jī moṃ ɠālhi kaī huī, uhā hīa āhe.
examples.en: This is the film I told you about.
Oh well, what's done is done.

grammar.title: Passing on what people said: ته
grammar.body:
To report what someone said, Sindhi puts **ته** (ta, 'that') after the speech verb and then repeats the words **as they were said** — like quoting without quotation marks:

هن چيو **ته** مان ٿڪل آهيان — lit. 'he said that I am tired' = he said he was tired.
**چيائين ته** رستي ۾ آهيان — he said he's on his way.

So the pronoun and the verb stay as the speaker used them: if your friend said 'I'll come', you report هن چيو ته **مان ايندس**. (You may also shift them as in English — هن چيو ته هو ايندو — but the 'as said' version is the most natural.)

**Questions:** پڇيو ته … + the question as asked: امان پڇيو ته **توهان ماني کاڌي؟** 'Mum asked if you'd eaten'.
**Orders and requests** keep the command form: امان چيو ته **جلدي گهر اچ** 'Mum said to come home early'.

**Useful verbs:** چوڻ (chayo 'said') · پڇڻ 'ask' · ٻڌائڻ 'tell' · خبر پوڻ 'find out': مون کي خبر پئي ته … 'I found out that …'. With the endings from Unit 16: **چيائين** 'he/she said', **چيم** 'I said'.

**Trap:** don't leave out ته — هن چيو مان ايندس sounds broken. And 'told **me**' needs کي: هن **مون کي** ٻڌايو ته …

examples.native: هن چيو ته مان ٿڪل آهيان.
examples.roman: hun chayo ta māṃ thakalu āhiyāṃ.
examples.en: He said he was tired. (lit. said: I am tired)

examples.native: امان پڇيو ته توهان ماني کاڌي؟
examples.roman: amāṃ puchhyo ta tavhāṃ mānī khādhī?
examples.en: Mum asked whether you'd eaten. (lit. asked: did you eat?)
He said he'd definitely come tomorrow.

examples.native: مون کيس چيو ته دير نه ڪر.
examples.roman: moṃ khesi chayo ta dera na karu.
examples.en: I told him not to be late. (lit. I said to him: don't be late)

examples.native: هن مون کي ٻڌايو ته امتحان ملتوي ٿي ويو آهي.
examples.roman: hun moṃ khe ɓudhāyo ta imtihānu multavī thī vayo āhe.
examples.en: She told me the exam has been postponed.

grammar.title: Telling it: first, then, suddenly — and "started to"
grammar.body:
**Putting events in order:**
پهريان pahiryāṃ — first · پوءِ poi — then · اوچتو ochito — suddenly · ان وقت / تڏهن — at that moment · انهيءَ ڪري inhīa kare — so, that's why · آخرڪار āxirkāra — in the end.

**Started to …:** oblique infinitive (-ṇa) + **لڳڻ**, which agrees with the subject like any intransitive past: هو **کلڻ لڳو** 'he started laughing', هوءَ **روئڻ لڳي** 'she started crying', اسين **کلڻ لڳاسين** 'we started laughing', مينهن **وسڻ لڳو** 'it started raining'.

**Keeping the chat going** (fillers): ڀلا 'so…' · يعني 'you mean…' · مطلب 'I mean' · اصل ۾ 'actually' · ٻڌ نه 'listen…' · خير 'anyway'.
**Reacting:** سچي؟ / واقعي؟ 'really?' · واهه! 'wow!' · ڪمال آهي! 'amazing!' · ويچارو! (f ويچاري!) 'poor thing!' · ڏاڍو افسوس ٿيو 'so sorry' · قسم سان! 'I swear!' · چرچو ٿو ڪرين؟ 'are you kidding?' · تڏهن ته! 'that explains it!'

With friends use **تون** and its short commands (ٻڌ، ٻڌاءِ، ڇڏ); with elders the same fillers work with **توهان**: ٻڌو نه، ٻڌايو.

examples.native: پهريان بس خراب ٿي، پوءِ مينهن به وسڻ لڳو.
examples.roman: pahiryāṃ basa xarābu thī, poi mīṃhu bi vasaṇa laɠo.
examples.en: First the bus broke down, then it started raining too.

examples.native: ٽرين دير سان آئي، انهيءَ ڪري مان دير سان پهتس.
examples.roman: ṭreni dera sāṃ āī, inhīa kare māṃ dera sāṃ pahutus.
examples.en: The train was late, that's why I got here late. (man)

examples.native: ٻڌو نه، مون کي هڪ ڳالهه ياد آئي.
examples.roman: ɓudho na, moṃ khe hika ɠālhi yāda āī.

dialogue.title: You will not believe who I sat next to
dialogue.setting: Sanam bumps into her friend Ayaz at a tea stall in Qasimabad, Hyderabad. He was supposed to be back from Karachi the night before.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: اياز! ڪالهه ڪٿي هئين؟ تو فون به نه کنيو!
lines.roman: ayāz! kālha kithe huyeṃ? to fon bi na khanyo!
lines.en: Ayaz! Where were you yesterday? You didn't even pick up!

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.en: Don't ask, it's a long story.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.en: So go on, tell me, what happened?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: مان ڪراچيءَ کان بس ۾ اچي رهيو هوس. جامشوري کان اڳ بس خراب ٿي پئي.
lines.roman: māṃ karāchīa khāṃ basa meṃ achī rahyo hos. jāmshore khāṃ aɠu basa xarābu thī paī.
lines.en: I was coming back from Karachi on the bus. Just before Jamshoro the bus broke down.

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: ٻه ڪلاڪ رستي تي ويٺا رهياسين. منهنجو فون به بند ٿي ويو.
lines.roman: ɓa kalāka raste te veṭhā rahyāsīṃ. munhinjo fon bi bandu thī vayo.
lines.en: We sat at the roadside for two hours. And my phone died.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: ويچارو! تڏهن ته تنهنجو فون بند هو.
lines.roman: vichāro! taɗahiṃ ta tunhinjo fon bandu ho.
lines.en: Poor you! So that's why your phone was off.

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: پر ٻڌ نه — جيڪو ماڻهو منهنجي ڀرسان ويٺو هو، سو اسان جو اسڪول وارو استاد هو!
lines.roman: para ɓudhu na — jeko māṇhū munhinjī bharsāṃ veṭho ho, so asāṃ jo iskūla vāro ustādu ho!
lines.en: But listen — the man sitting next to me was our old schoolteacher!

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.en: No way! Did he recognise you?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: ها! چيائين ته تون اڃا به دير سان ٿو اچين!
lines.roman: hā! chayāīṃ ta tūṃ añā bi dera sāṃ tho acheṃ!
lines.en: Yes! He said, "You're still late for everything!"

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: هاهاها! واهه، ڪمال آهي! پوءِ گهر ڪڏهن پهتين؟
lines.roman: hāhāhā! vāh, kamālu āhe! poi ghara kaɗahiṃ pahuteṃ?
lines.en: Hahaha! That's brilliant! So when did you get home?

lines.speaker: Ayaz
lines.native: آخرڪار ٻي بس آئي، ۽ رات جو ٻارهين وڳي پهتس. خير، ڳالهه ختم!
lines.roman: āxirkāra ɓī basa āī, ai rāti jo ɓārahīṃ vaɠe pahutus. xairu, ɠālhi xatmu!
lines.en: Finally another bus came, and I got home at midnight. Anyway, end of story!

culture:
Sindhis love to talk, and the **ڪچهري** — friends or relatives sitting together for hours over tea, swapping news and stories — is the heart of social life. In villages it happens in the **اوطاق** (otāq), the men's guest room; in Hyderabad and Karachi it happens at tea stalls, on rooftops, in hostel rooms and in endless WhatsApp voice notes. A good story is told with lots of **پوءِ** and **ٻڌ نه**, and the listener's job is to keep it going: **سچي؟**, **پوءِ؟**, **ويچارو!**, **واهه!**.

Among friends people use **تون** and **يار**, and often mix in Urdu and English (**سيريئسلي؟**, **ٽينشن نه وٺ**), especially in Karachi. With older people you switch to **توهان**, **ادا / ادي** or **سائين**, and keep the fillers polite: **ٻڌو نه**, **جي، واقعي؟** Calling an elder **يار** would be rude.

Sindhi sounds a little different from place to place: **Vicholi**, spoken around Hyderabad, is the basis of the standard; upper Sindh (Sukkur, Larkana) speaks **Siroli**, lower Sindh (Thatta, Badin) **Lari**, and Thar its own dialect close to Marwari — but everyone understands **سچي؟** and **ڳالهه ختم!**

tip.title: First, then, suddenly… started to: لڳڻ
tip.body:
- Order events with **پهريان** 'first', **پوءِ** 'then', **اوچتو** 'suddenly', **انهيءَ ڪري** 'so', **آخرڪار** 'in the end'.
- 'Started to …' = verb-ṇa + **لڳڻ**, agreeing with the subject: هو کلڻ **لڳو** · هوءَ روئڻ **لڳي** · اسين کلڻ **لڳاسين**.

sentences.roman: kālha āfīsa meṃ hika mazedāra ɠālhi thī.
sentences.en: Something funny happened at the office yesterday.

sentences.en: Suddenly the power went and everyone started laughing.

sentences.roman: ɓāru roaṇa laɠo, inhīa kare asīṃ jaldī ghara moṭyāsīṃ.

sentences.roman: asīṃ sabhu khilaṇa laɠāsīṃ.

sentences.native: آخرڪار رات جو ٻارهين وڳي گهر پهتاسين.

sentences.en: In the end we got home at midnight.

sentences.roman: hī chhā qiso āhe?
sentences.en: What's going on here?

tip.title: Really? Wow! Poor thing!
tip.body:
- **سچي؟** is the friendly 'really?'; **واقعي؟** works with anyone.
- **واهه!** / **ڪمال آهي!** for good news; **ڏاڍو افسوس ٿيو** for bad news.
- **ويچارو!** agrees with the person: ويچارو (a man) · **ويچاري** (a woman) · **ويچارا** (people).

sentences.native: سچي؟ هو دبئي هليو ويو؟
sentences.roman: sachī? hū dubaī halyo vayo?
sentences.en: Really? He's gone off to Dubai?

sentences.native: واقعي؟ تو ڪالهه هن کي ڏٺو؟
sentences.roman: vāqaʿī? to kālha hun khe ɗiṭho?
sentences.en: Really? You saw him yesterday?

sentences.native: واهه! توکي نوڪري ملي وئي؟
sentences.roman: vāh! tokhe nokirī milī vaī?
sentences.en: Wow! You got the job?

sentences.native: ڪمال جو ماڻهو آهي!
sentences.roman: kamāla jo māṇhū āhe!
sentences.en: He's an amazing guy!

sentences.native: اها ته عجيب ڳالهه آهي!
sentences.roman: uhā ta ʿajību ɠālhi āhe!
sentences.en: Now that's weird!

sentences.native: ويچاري! هن جو فون چوري ٿي ويو.
sentences.roman: vichārī! hun jo fon chorī thī vayo.
sentences.en: Poor girl! Her phone got stolen.

sentences.native: ويچارو سڄي رات سمهي نه سگهيو.
sentences.roman: vichāro saʄī rāti sumhī na saghyo.
sentences.en: Poor guy, he couldn't sleep all night.

sentences.native: ويچارا ٻار ٻه ڪلاڪ بس ۾ ويٺا رهيا.
sentences.roman: vichārā ɓāra ɓa kalāka basa meṃ veṭhā rahyā.
sentences.en: The poor kids sat in the bus for two hours.

sentences.native: مون کي ڏاڍو افسوس آهي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe ɗāḍho afsosu āhe.
sentences.en: I'm really sorry.

sentences.native: واقعي؟ مون کي ته خبر ئي نه هئي!
sentences.roman: vāqaʿī? moṃ khe ta xabara ī na huī!
sentences.en: Really? I had no idea!

lessons.title: The one who…, the place where…

tip.title: جيڪو … سو — the one who … he
tip.body:
- Say it in two halves: **جيڪو** ماڻهو آيو، **سو** منهنجو دوست آهي.
- Both words agree: جيڪو … سو (m) · **جيڪا … سا** (f) · **جيڪي … سي** (pl).
- Same idea: **جتي … اتي** 'where … there', **جڏهن … تڏهن** 'when … then'.
- Never the question words ڪير / ڪڏهن here.

new: جيڪو ماڻهو ڪالهه آيو هو، سو منهنجو چاچو آهي.

sentences.native: جيڪو ڇوڪرو بس ۾ مليو هو، سو ڪير هو؟
sentences.roman: jeko chhokiro basa meṃ milyo ho, so ker ho?
sentences.en: Who was that boy we met on the bus?

sentences.native: جيڪا ڇوڪري توهان سان ڳالهائي رهي هئي، سا منهنجي دوست آهي.
sentences.roman: jekā chhokirī tavhāṃ sāṃ ɠālhāe rahī huī, sā munhinjī dosta āhe.
sentences.en: The girl who was talking to you is my friend.

sentences.native: جيڪي ماڻهو دير سان آيا، سي ٻاهر ويٺا آهن.
sentences.roman: jeke māṇhū dera sāṃ āyā, se ɓāhari veṭhā āhin.
sentences.en: The people who came late are sitting outside.

sentences.native: جڏهن پهچين، تڏهن فون ڪر.
sentences.roman: jaɗahiṃ pahucheṃ, taɗahiṃ fon karu.
sentences.en: Call me when you get there. (informal)

sentences.native: جيڪو توهان کي وڻي، سو وٺو.
sentences.roman: jeko tavhāṃ khe vaṇe, so vaṭho.
sentences.en: Take whatever you like.

sentences.native: جتي ڪالهه وياسين، اتي ٻيهر هلون؟
sentences.roman: jite kālha vayāsīṃ, ute ɓiyahar halūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall we go back to where we went yesterday?

sentences.native: جيئن تون چوين.
sentences.roman: jīeṃ tūṃ chaveṃ.
sentences.en: Whatever you say. (informal)

sentences.native: مون کيس ڪونه سڃاتو، ڏاڍو ٿلهو ٿي ويو آهي!
sentences.roman: moṃ khesi kona sañāto, ɗāḍho thulho thī vayo āhe!
sentences.en: I didn't recognise him, he's put on so much weight!

sentences.native: توهان مون کي سڃاتو؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ moṃ khe sañāto?
sentences.en: Do you recognise me? (polite)

tip.title: He said that…: چيو ته + the words as said
tip.body:
- Report speech with **ته** and the speaker's own words: هن چيو **ته** مان پهچان ٿو 'he said he's arriving'.
- Questions and orders stay as they were: امان چيو ته جلدي گهر **اچ**.
- Found out: مون کي خبر **پئي** ته … (خبر is f).

sentences.native: هن چيو ته مان پنجن منٽن ۾ پهچان ٿو.
sentences.roman: hun chayo ta māṃ panjan minaṭan meṃ pahuchāṃ tho.
sentences.en: He said he'd be there in five minutes.

sentences.native: امان چيو ته جلدي گهر اچ.
sentences.roman: amāṃ chayo ta jaldī ghara achu.
sentences.en: Mum said to come home early.

sentences.native: هوءَ پڇي رهي هئي ته تون ڪڏهن ايندين.
sentences.roman: hūa puchhī rahī huī ta tūṃ kaɗahiṃ endeṃ.
sentences.en: She was asking when you'd come.

sentences.native: مون کي ڪالهه خبر پئي ته هن جي شادي آهي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe kālha xabara paī ta hun jī shādī āhe.
sentences.en: I found out yesterday that he's getting married.

sentences.native: توکي ڪيئن خبر پئي؟
sentences.roman: tokhe kīeṃ xabara paī?
sentences.en: How did you find out?

sentences.native: قسم سان، هن پاڻ چيو ته مان نه ايندس.
sentences.roman: qasama sāṃ, hun pāṇa chayo ta māṃ na endus.
sentences.en: I swear, he said himself he wouldn't come.

sentences.native: مون چيو ته هرو ڀرو پريشان نه ٿيو.
sentences.roman: moṃ chayo ta haro bharo pareshānu na thiyo.
sentences.en: I said don't worry for nothing.

sentences.native: چيائين ته ٽڪيٽون مون وٽ آهن.
sentences.roman: chayāīṃ ta ṭikeṭūṃ moṃ vaṭi āhin.
sentences.en: He said he's got the tickets.

sentences.native: هرو ڀرو ڪوڙ نه ڳالهاءِ.
sentences.roman: haro bharo kūṛu na ɠālhāi.
sentences.en: Don't lie for no reason. (informal)

lessons.title: Keeping the chat going

tip.title: So…, I mean…, actually…
tip.body:
- **ڀلا** opens a question softly; **يعني** checks you understood: يعني تون نه ايندين؟
- **مطلب** / **منهنجو مطلب آهي ته** 'I mean'; **اصل ۾** 'actually'.
- **يار** and **ٻڌ نه** are for friends; with elders say **ٻڌو نه** and **جي**.

new: ٻڌ نه، هڪ مزيدار ڳالهه ٻڌايان.

sentences.native: يار، اڄ رات ڪچهري ڪريون؟
sentences.roman: yār, aʄu rāti kachahrī karyūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall we get together for a chat tonight, man?

sentences.native: يعني تون نه ايندين؟
sentences.roman: yaʿnī tūṃ na endeṃ?
sentences.en: So you mean you're not coming?

sentences.native: منهنجو مطلب هو ته اڄ نه، سڀاڻي.
sentences.roman: munhinjo matlabu ho ta aʄu na, subhāṇe.
sentences.en: What I meant was not today — tomorrow.

sentences.native: اصل ۾ مون کي وقت ئي ڪونه هو.
sentences.roman: asula meṃ moṃ khe vaqtu ī kona ho.
sentences.en: Actually, I just didn't have time.

sentences.native: سچ پچ، تنهنجي ڳالهه صحيح آهي.
sentences.roman: sach pach, tunhinjī ɠālhi sahī āhe.
sentences.en: Honestly, you've got a point.

sentences.native: ٻڌ نه يار، اڄ ڇا ڪيو؟
sentences.roman: ɓudhu na yār, aʄu chhā kayo?
sentences.en: So, man, what did you get up to today?

sentences.native: ڪچهريءَ ۾ ٽي ڪلاڪ گذري ويا.
sentences.roman: kachahrīa meṃ ṭī kalāka guzrī vayā.
sentences.en: Three hours flew by chatting.

sentences.native: اسان جي ڪچهري رات جو دير تائين هلي.
sentences.roman: asāṃ jī kachahrī rāti jo dera tāīṃ halī.
sentences.en: Our chat went on late into the night.

sentences.native: ڀلا، يعني سڀ ٺيڪ آهي؟
sentences.roman: bhalā, yaʿnī sabhu ṭhīku āhe?
sentences.en: So everything's fine, then?

sentences.native: مطلب، مون کي پڪ ناهي.
sentences.roman: matlabu, moṃ khe paka nāhe.
sentences.en: I mean, I'm not sure.

lessons.title: Joking around

tip.title: Kidding: چرچو ڪرڻ
tip.body:
- **چرچو ڪرڻ** = to joke: مان چرچو پيو ڪريان 'I'm only kidding'.
- **ڇڏ يار** 'forget it, man' — only with friends.
- **ڳالهه ختم!** closes a story or an argument.

new: سچ پچ، مون کي کل اچي وئي.

sentences.native: مان چرچو پيو ڪريان، يار!
sentences.roman: māṃ charcho peyo karyāṃ, yār!
sentences.en: I'm just kidding, man!

sentences.native: چرچا نه ڪر، سچ ٻڌاءِ.
sentences.roman: charchā na karu, sachu ɓudhāi.
sentences.en: Stop joking, tell me the truth. (informal)

sentences.native: هو هر ڳالهه تي چرچا ڪندو آهي.
sentences.roman: hū har ɠālhi te charchā kando āhe.
sentences.en: He jokes about everything.

sentences.native: ڇڏ يار، هاڻي ڪجهه ٻيو ڳالهايون.
sentences.roman: chhaɗu yār, hāṇe kujhu ɓiyo ɠālhāyūṃ.
sentences.en: Forget it, man, let's talk about something else.

sentences.native: ٺيڪ آهي، ڳالهه ختم. هاڻي ماني کائون؟
sentences.roman: ṭhīku āhe, ɠālhi xatmu. hāṇe mānī khāūṃ?
sentences.en: OK, that's that. Shall we eat now?

sentences.native: ڇا ڳالهه آهي، اڄ ڏاڍو خوش آهين!
sentences.roman: chhā ɠālhi āhe, aʄu ɗāḍho xushu āhīṃ!
sentences.en: What's up — you're very happy today!

sentences.native: سچ پچ، مون کي ڪجهه به ياد ناهي.
sentences.roman: sach pach, moṃ khe kujhu bi yāda nāhe.
sentences.en: Honestly, I don't remember a thing.

sentences.native: سڀ ٻار کلڻ لڳا.
sentences.roman: sabhu ɓāra khilaṇa laɠā.
sentences.en: All the kids started laughing.
